hero.name: Mariam Amiri
hero.description: I am Mariam Amiri, a writer and young leader dedicated to empowering girls and young people through writing and ideas.

homeAbout.description: I am Mariam Amiri, a writer, storyteller, and a voice for what is too often left unheard. My journey began with words, but it did not end there. For me, words are tools for illuminating darkness, reflecting realities, and building bridges between individual experiences and collective concerns. At the intersection of writing, leadership, and advocacy, I strive to keep stories alive that deserve to be heard—stories of hope, resilience, and change. I believe that every story, when told with care, can spark awareness and inspire movement toward a more just future. Today, I am walking a path that goes beyond expression and leads toward impact; a path where voices are not silenced and words become catalysts for transformation. This is a space to see, listen, and rethink—a place where stories remain alive.

hero.title: Life Through the Mirror of Words
hero.description: Maryam Amiri, a Hazara writer and young leader; a storyteller of human experiences and a voice for hope, justice, and change. Through writing and advocacy, I strive to be a voice for young people and build a bridge between individual stories and social concerns.

story.title: My Journey
paragraphs: I am Maryam Amiri, eighteen years old. So far, I have published more than 360 articles in four languages across seventeen national and international media outlets. My first book, "A Different Ending for a New Beginning," was published by Shisha Media and tells the story of a girl who is deprived of education but never gives up.

I was selected as the Afghanistan Branch Leader of the American Young Writers Initiatives Magazine and founded the first branch of the organization in my country. I also served as the Head of the Writing Department at Cluster Education, where I worked with many girls. Together, we founded the Young Writers Association and held workshops with WrightGirls USA to strengthen the literary skills of girls.

Beyond writing, I have also participated in global leadership and advocacy programs. I received the Whetstone Legislative Advocacy Fellowship and worked with young people from 31 countries on human rights. I participated in the Nobel program for six months, collaborating with young people from 160 countries. I was selected as one of the change leaders in Thailand and hosted international writers during the "Eleven Days of Global Unity." On October 12, 2025, I received the Women's Empowerment Award from the British Millennium Council.

I have participated as a distinguished delegate at the 13th Asia World Model United Nations Conference (AWMUN XIII) and as a guest speaker at the PDEU Youth Parliament and HFF 2026. These honors are not merely medals; they are steps toward building a brighter future for girls. Today, I am honored to have reached the final stage of the Annual Exceptional Women of Peace Award, an award that reflects my commitment to justice, empowerment, and change.

timeline.title: My Educational and Professional Journey
timeline.description: Educational and professional journey across Afghanistan — Kabul, Herat, and Mazar

education.title: Student
education.description: I graduated from Bal Parwaz Online School in December 2025 after completing grade 12.

education.title: Cluster Education Student
education.description: As part of my education at Cluster Education, I studied five academic subjects and also participated in empowerment classes. During this period, I joined the global Peace Game on Earth by 2030 campaign with a five-person team and participated in group projects aimed at connecting young people's voices with collective action and creating meaningful change.

education.title: High School Program
education.description: I recently began my academic studies at Forward International Academy, an American school, and am following the American high school curriculum.

education.title: Level Two and Level Three Student
education.description: I completed Level 2 of the British school curriculum at EBA and am currently progressing through Level 3.

education.title: Whetstone Fellowship
education.description: Through the Whetstone Fellowship, I worked with participants from 31 countries in legal and political fields. The program provided an opportunity for exchanging perspectives, shared learning, and developing advocacy skills at an international level.

education.title: University of Cambridge
education.description: I received a scholarship to take the courses "Democratizing Education for Global Justice and Sustainability" and "Key Foundations: Trade Law, Sustainable Development and Rights" at the University of Cambridge. This program provided a valuable opportunity for deeper learning, exchanging perspectives, and developing leadership skills in educational justice, global sustainability, law, and trade.

education.title: Participant
education.description: I participated in the Aspire Program, which focuses on leadership, teamwork, and personal growth. Through participation in group leadership projects, I strengthened my collaborative leadership, effective cooperation, and personal development skills. This experience provided a valuable opportunity for practical learning and creating positive change in collective environments.

experience.title: Young Writers Association Leader
experience.description: For one year, I led the Young Writers Association with the participation of 250 Afghan girls and helped them share their life stories through national and international media. The program included in-person and online sessions with girls from different provinces of Afghanistan, as well as from Iran and Pakistan. Our association's main focus was storytelling and documenting history — an effort to preserve individual and collective experiences and make them part of literary and social memory.

experience.title: Afghan Women's Empowerment
experience.description: I participated in WriteGirls creative writing workshops, a program supporting young women in developing storytelling and self-expression skills. The Young Writers Association also joined these workshops, allowing its members to benefit from the creative training. This collaboration provided a valuable opportunity to strengthen the literary empowerment of Afghan girls and create a space for storytelling and documenting their experiences.

experience.title: Empowered Future Minds
experience.organization: Katrina Biloruska Foundation & Cyprus Business School
experience.description: Our project, called FeminStem, was developed as an initiative with a group of girls from different countries. We worked as a team to strengthen our scientific and practical skills in STEM and develop innovative approaches to online learning. FeminStem was not only a platform for personal and academic growth, but also an opportunity to build solidarity among girls from different cultures and countries and turn knowledge into collective action.

memberships.title: Memberships & Collaborations
items: I signed the Women's Empowerment Principles (WEPs) Statement of Support – United Nations on April 30, 2026, representing girls. This action marked the beginning of my collaboration with the United Nations in support of girls, as part of my commitment to empowering women and girls, advancing educational justice, and creating equal opportunities.

I serve as the Editor of the Publications Department at Education Bridge for Afghanistan. In this role, I am responsible for guiding educational and literary content, managing writing teams and publications, and strengthening the capacity of young people in storytelling and publishing.

Member of the United States Association for the United Nations (UNA-USA) – a national movement with more than 20,000 active members across more than 230 community and university chapters, supporting strong cooperation between the United States and the United Nations.

I work as a "Changemaker" at Seema Academy and contribute to the organization's educational campaigns. In this role, I am responsible for designing and implementing seven- to twelve-day educational campaigns aimed at empowering young people, strengthening leadership skills, and creating positive change in society.
